When there is a real trade-off—for example, an option that maximizes growth or profit but weakens people, community, or the environment—what would “harmony” ask you to do differently?

Well they say there are no solutions there are only trade-offs so change is a process which takes time and we need to balance trade-offs with a timeline because in many instances it may be the case that the person needs to make money first in order to make the change they need what they want to create with their vehicle or whatever it is but we should do that with the least possible impact on people community and the environment you know but I you know I would risk saying there's a hard line you cannot weaken people community or environment never but the thing is that in the world we're in this transitional state you know there's no real way to do a hard stop on anything that we're doing right now because it would even if it would improve the environment it would weaken people for example gasoline we can stop gas and crude oil extraction and refinement people for a while and community for a while would be struggling until we move to renewable fuels you ever say like there's it's it's over time the the goal is to strengthen people community and the environment in that transitional phase needs to be handled with care you know not with bullshit beating around the bush but it needs to be done in a way that you know the altruistic goal of just getting rid of all this bad stuff in the world will still create a hard transition and so do we need to go through the hard transition sometimes yes but we can also find a way that makes it a lot easier simpler safer you know so there's that that balance that's what harmony is in my world in my view
